strengths: The framework addresses a practical problem relevant to NLP research on language models for code. Its staged integration of localization, repair, repository context, and execution feedback is coherent, and escalating effort after unsuccessful repairs is a sensible design.

Experimental coverage is substantial: four benchmarks, three programming languages, and seven backbones for UniDebugger-Lite. The reported 197 correct Defects4J repairs versus ChatRepair’s 157, together with consistent plausible-repair improvements on ConDefects, suggest a potentially useful contribution.

The appendix provides agent prompts, pseudocode, and detailed examples, and the manuscript supplies a source-code link. Distinguishing plausible from correct repairs and replacing web search with local retrieval during evaluation are useful methodological choices.
weaknesses: The decisive concern is repair validation. Figure 23’s supposedly successful Lang-1 patch checks the last significant hexadecimal digit for overflow, using offsets +7 and +15. For the paper’s own failing input, 0x80000000 (Figure 16), it consequently selects createInteger and still throws NumberFormatException. A Java check of the transcribed branch confirms this failure. This could be an illustration error, but it directly contradicts Appendix A.4’s success claim; the actual evaluated patch and test results need reconciliation.

Important numerical inconsistencies undermine confidence in the reported evaluation. Table 1 gives 286 plausible Defects4J repairs, whereas Tables 2 and 4 give 291 for the full configuration without explaining a different run or protocol. Table 1 also reports 90 correct but only 75 plausible repairs for RewardRepair, contradicting the stated definitions. These require a reconciled account of configurations, evaluated bugs, and outcomes.

The experiments do not isolate the contribution of hierarchical coordination. Adding agents also adds model calls, information, tools, and repair opportunities. There is no controlled comparison against an iterative single-agent system with the same backbone, tools, and budget, or against always invoking L3. Moreover, a multi-agent debugging attempt is not equivalent to one baseline patch sample, so fewer reported attempts do not establish superior cost efficiency. Comparable total tokens, calls, execution costs, and repair success are needed.

The end-to-end claim and execution protocol remain insufficiently specified. Algorithm 1 assumes a bug-located file, but the procedure for selecting this file from test failures is only informally described; this does not establish that ground-truth files were used, but leaves the localization boundary unclear. The algorithm also returns unconditionally at line 54 inside its outer retry loop, preventing subsequent iterations as written. Exact model versions, decoding settings, the resampling limit m, and local retrieval configuration need specification.

Correctness and robustness evidence needs strengthening. The manuscript does not specify the manual correctness criterion or inspection protocol underlying the 197 correct repairs. ConDefects comparisons and agent ablations report only plausibility, while Codeflaws correctness estimates rely on 100 sampled plausible patches per evaluated configuration. Sample identifiers, uncertainty estimates, and repeated-run variability would make these results more assessable. The current evidence supports test-suite success more clearly than the broader claims about reliable debugging.
